description: Overlapping editorial functions in a paragraph, not topics, truth tests or quality scores. No target balance and no forced primary label.

labels.label: Technical
labels.definition: Explains a formal definition, algorithm, implementation, measurable constraint or how a mechanism produces an effect. A code name alone is not enough.

labels.label: Embodied / instructional
labels.definition: Invites or directs a concrete bodily, sensory or interface action, including looking, moving, pressing, drawing or making an actionable comparison. Second-person address alone is not enough.

labels.label: Inquiry / discovery
labels.definition: Stages a genuine question, unresolved puzzle, tentative hypothesis, discrepancy or experiment for the reader to investigate. Not every declarative explanation or rhetorical question qualifies.

labels.label: Critical
labels.definition: Examines assumptions, norms, authority, exclusions, interests or the stakes of choices built into a representation, algorithm or institution. A technical limit or surprising behavior alone is insufficient unless its assumptions or consequences are questioned.

labels.label: Poetic
labels.definition: Makes meaning through evocative imagery, metaphor, personification, rhythm, compression or deliberate resonance. Merely mentioning art or using a technical metaphor does not suffice. This is a mode of language, not a quality judgment.

labels.label: Contextual / scholarly
labels.definition: Locates the encounter in an artistic, historical, philosophical or documentary source; explains attribution, a relation to that source, or the limits of the comparison. Earlier hall callbacks alone are connective instead.

labels.label: Connective
labels.definition: Substantively recaps earlier learning, bridges halls or concepts, negotiates scope or pace, or prepares the next encounter. Mere conjunctions or local sentence flow are insufficient.

labels.label: Interpretive
labels.definition: Offers or weighs a possible aesthetic, symbolic or philosophical reading of an encounter. A technical explanation, source attribution or evocative word alone is insufficient. Can overlap critical or poetic without being identical to either.
